title: Sunshine Gardens in Saginaw and jobs in Flint and Lansing
summary: Small joints with Choker Campbell and Jimmy Parker; the date is 1941, when Jones was turned down for service for flat feet.

blocks.x: What about Sunshine Gardens in Saginaw?
Well, Sunshine Gardens was one of those little joints. You have to call it a joint because it was. They had a band there; we used to work there occasionally.

When I was there, I worked with a guy named… A saxophone player named Choker. I don't know what his first name was but we used to call him Choker. I think it was Choker Campbell. He was a tenor saxophone player, and Jimmy Parker. They were both in that band. Now, Jimmy is the saxophone player that we had in the small band in Pontiac who played every instrument in the band. We worked in Flint Michigan, and Saginaw – he didn't work with us in Lansing, but he did work with us in Saginaw.
We are at the point that we are talking about 1918, 1930. Well, 1918 was when you were born. So I'm trying to get to 1934, 35, 36. Had the depression ended?
This was 1941, because the war was on at the time. They turned me down because I had flat feet. I wasn't good enough. That was when we worked in Saginaw and Flint.
